rival_explanations: The pole is a token-identity neuron keyed on a fixed set of frequent code tokens ('retch', 'Property', 'Settings', '_key', '.Property'), so it should fire on those tokens wherever they occur, including as standalone words in prose, and should not fire on other pieces of the same identifiers.

The pole is a generic word-piece continuation detector that fires on any token glued to the previous token inside a multi-token word, so ordinary prose splits and invented compounds ('pan'+'es', 'international'+'ization', 'fooProperty') should fire as strongly as real code identifiers.

The pole is a lookahead neuron that prepares the delimiter closing the current expression, so it should fire on any token immediately before a ';', a ')' or a newline regardless of whether that token sits inside a compound name (the Jacobian lens promotes closing quotes, parens and newlines, which fits this reading).
